claim: High-resolution isoelectric focusing HiRIEF LC-MS/MS demonstrates high proteome coverage for human plasma proteome analysis.
source: Here, we present a method for in-depth human plasma proteome analysis based on high-resolution isoelectric focusing HiRIEF LC-MS/MS, demonstrating high proteome coverage, reproducibility and the potential for liquid biopsy protein profiling.
evidence: The abstract states this as a primary finding of the study, supported by the experimental data presented throughout the manuscript.

claim: High-resolution isoelectric focusing HiRIEF LC-MS/MS demonstrates reproducibility for human plasma proteome analysis.
source: Here, we present a method for in-depth human plasma proteome analysis based on high-resolution isoelectric focusing HiRIEF LC-MS/MS, demonstrating high proteome coverage, reproducibility and the potential for liquid biopsy protein profiling.
evidence: The abstract states this as a primary finding, with reproducibility data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 6 and 7.

claim: The HiRIEF LC-MS/MS method has potential for liquid biopsy protein profiling.
source: Here, we present a method for in-depth human plasma proteome analysis based on high-resolution isoelectric focusing HiRIEF LC-MS/MS, demonstrating high proteome coverage, reproducibility and the potential for liquid biopsy protein profiling.
evidence: The abstract states this as a conclusion based on the method's capabilities demonstrated in the study.

claim: Integrating genomic sequence information to MS-based plasma proteome analysis enables detection of single amino acid variants.
source: By integrating genomic sequence information to the MS-based plasma proteome analysis, we enable detection of single amino acid variants and for the first time demonstrate transfer of multiple protein variants between mother and fetus across the placenta.
evidence: The abstract states this as a primary finding, with supporting data in the proteogenomics section showing detection of 229 SAAV peptides.

claim: Transfer of multiple protein variants between mother and fetus across the placenta has been demonstrated for the first time.
source: By integrating genomic sequence information to the MS-based plasma proteome analysis, we enable detection of single amino acid variants and for the first time demonstrate transfer of multiple protein variants between mother and fetus across the placenta.
evidence: The abstract explicitly states this is the first demonstration, supported by proteogenomics data showing 21 proteins with evidence of transfer.

claim: The HiRIEF method can detect low abundance tissue-annotated proteins in plasma.
source: We further show that our method has the ability to detect both low abundance tissue-annotated proteins and phosphorylated proteins in plasma, as well as quantitate differences in plasma proteomes between the mother and the newborn as well as changes related to pregnancy.
evidence: The abstract states this capability, with Figure 3 showing detection of over 500 tissue-enriched proteins.

claim: The HiRIEF method can detect phosphorylated proteins in plasma.
source: We further show that our method has the ability to detect both low abundance tissue-annotated proteins and phosphorylated proteins in plasma, as well as quantitate differences in plasma proteomes between the mother and the newborn as well as changes related to pregnancy.
evidence: The abstract states this capability, with data showing 3.3% of proteins containing phosphorylated peptides.

claim: The HiRIEF method can quantitate differences in plasma proteomes between mother and newborn.
source: We further show that our method has the ability to detect both low abundance tissue-annotated proteins and phosphorylated proteins in plasma, as well as quantitate differences in plasma proteomes between the mother and the newborn as well as changes related to pregnancy.
evidence: The abstract states this capability, with Figure 4 showing comparative analysis of mother-newborn pairs.

claim: The HiRIEF method can quantitate changes in plasma proteomes related to pregnancy.
source: We further show that our method has the ability to detect both low abundance tissue-annotated proteins and phosphorylated proteins in plasma, as well as quantitate differences in plasma proteomes between the mother and the newborn as well as changes related to pregnancy.
evidence: The abstract states this capability, with Figure 4b showing comparison of pre-pregnancy and third trimester samples.

claim: The Plasma Proteome Database (PPD) is an example of meta-analysis of publicly available plasma proteomics datasets.
source: Due to major analytical challenges in plasma, extensive MS-based plasma proteome studies have largely focused on meta-analysis of publicly available datasets. Examples include the Plasma Proteome Database (PPD) (Nanjappa et al., 2014) and the PeptideAtlas plasma proteome repository (Schwenk et al., 2017).
evidence: The text cites the PPD as an example of meta-analysis approaches in plasma proteomics.

claim: The PeptideAtlas plasma proteome repository is an example of meta-analysis of publicly available plasma proteomics datasets.
source: Due to major analytical challenges in plasma, extensive MS-based plasma proteome studies have largely focused on meta-analysis of publicly available datasets. Examples include the Plasma Proteome Database (PPD) (Nanjappa et al., 2014) and the PeptideAtlas plasma proteome repository (Schwenk et al., 2017).
evidence: The text cites PeptideAtlas as an example of meta-analysis approaches in plasma proteomics.

claim: The plasma PeptideAtlas compiles 178 MS datasets describing a total of 3509 proteins in plasma.
source: The recently curated plasma PeptideAtlas now compiles 178 MS datasets, to describe a total of 3509 proteins in plasma, including important in-depth plasma proteomics data-sets from recent years (Keshishian et al., 2015; Geyer et al., 2016a; Geyer et al., 2016b) illustrating state of the art of proteome-wide MS-based plasma proteomics.
evidence: The text provides specific numbers from the PeptideAtlas database compilation.

claim: A major challenge in plasma proteomics is the ability to analyze larger sample cohorts while retaining proteome coverage.
source: One major challenge in plasma proteomics is the ability to analyze larger sample cohorts while retaining proteome coverage.
evidence: The text explicitly identifies this as a major challenge in the field.

claim: Plasma datasets are often characterized by a high proportion of one-peptide identifications resulting in poor overlap between analyses.
source: Plasma datasets are often characterized by a high proportion of one-peptide identifications resulting in poor overlap between analyses.
evidence: The text states this as a known characteristic of plasma proteomics datasets.

claim: In the Plasma Proteome Database, 10,546 proteins have been reported from 509 publications.
source: For example, in the Plasma Proteome Database 10 546 proteins have been reported from 509 publications; however, only 3784 of the identified proteins are present in two or more studies (Nanjappa et al., 2014).
evidence: The text cites specific numbers from the Plasma Proteome Database.

claim: Only 3,784 of the identified proteins in the Plasma Proteome Database are present in two or more studies.
source: For example, in the Plasma Proteome Database 10 546 proteins have been reported from 509 publications; however, only 3784 of the identified proteins are present in two or more studies (Nanjappa et al., 2014).
evidence: The text cites this statistic to illustrate poor overlap between studies.

claim: Roughly 55% of the total protein mass in plasma is made up by albumin alone.
source: Roughly 55% of the total protein mass in plasma is made up by albumin alone and as few as seven proteins together make up 85% of the total protein mass.
evidence: The text states this as a known characteristic of plasma composition.

claim: As few as seven proteins together make up 85% of the total protein mass in plasma.
source: Roughly 55% of the total protein mass in plasma is made up by albumin alone and as few as seven proteins together make up 85% of the total protein mass.
evidence: The text states this as a known characteristic of plasma composition.

claim: 2,300 housekeeping proteins are thought to make up 75% of the protein mass in tissue and cellular data.
source: This can be compared with estimates from tissue and cellular data where 2300 housekeeping proteins are thought to make up 75% of the protein mass (Kim et al., 2014).
evidence: The text cites this estimate from tissue/cellular studies for comparison with plasma.

claim: High plasma proteome coverage is dependent on extensive fractionation.
source: In general, high plasma proteome coverage is dependent on extensive fractionation.
evidence: The text states this as a general principle in plasma proteomics.

claim: Aiming for high number of identified proteins comes at the cost of low sample throughput and vice versa.
source: Consequently, aiming for high number of identified proteins comes at the cost of low sample throughput and vice versa.
evidence: The text describes this as a trade-off in plasma proteomics methodology.

claim: 342 proteins were monitored in 230 samples in a longitudinal study of twins using SWATH-MS.
source: Examples of high-throughput studies include 342 proteins monitored in 230 samples in a longitudinal study of twins using SWATH-MS (Liu et al., 2015) or relative quantification of 146 proteins in 500 subjects using iTRAQ labeling (5% peptide FDR) (Cole et al., 2013).
evidence: The text cites this as an example of a high-throughput plasma proteomics study.

claim: Relative quantification of 146 proteins in 500 subjects was achieved using iTRAQ labeling.
source: Examples of high-throughput studies include 342 proteins monitored in 230 samples in a longitudinal study of twins using SWATH-MS (Liu et al., 2015) or relative quantification of 146 proteins in 500 subjects using iTRAQ labeling (5% peptide FDR) (Cole et al., 2013).
evidence: The text cites this as an example of a high-throughput plasma proteomics study.

claim: 285 proteins were quantified from 10 plasma samples in as little as 3 hr analysis time per sample.
source: Efforts to increase the throughput by shortening the analysis time of shotgun MS have also been made, for example by quantifying 285 proteins from 10 plasma samples in as little as 3 hr analysis time/sample (Geyer et al., 2016a).
evidence: The text cites this as an example of efforts to increase throughput.

claim: A longitudinal study with 43 patients followed over 12 months detected on average 437 proteins per individual from 319 plasma samples measured in quadruplicates.
source: The same technology was later applied to a longitudinal study with 43 patients followed over 12 months, making in total 319 plasma samples measured in quadruplicates (a total of 1294 samples), detecting on average 437 proteins per individual (Geyer et al., 2016b).
evidence: The text cites this study as an example of high-throughput plasma proteomics.

claim: A study by Keshishian et al. reported in total over 5,000 proteins from 16 plasma samples using high pH reversed phase separation in combination with iTRAQ 4-plex labeling.
source: In 2015, a study by Keshishian et al. (2015) reported in total over 5000 proteins from 16 plasma samples using high pH reversed phase separation in combination with iTRAQ 4-plex labeling, making it the single most comprehensive plasma proteomics study to-date.
evidence: The text cites this as the most comprehensive plasma proteomics study at the time.

claim: The Keshishian et al. study is the single most comprehensive plasma proteomics study to-date.
source: In 2015, a study by Keshishian et al. (2015) reported in total over 5000 proteins from 16 plasma samples using high pH reversed phase separation in combination with iTRAQ 4-plex labeling, making it the single most comprehensive plasma proteomics study to-date.
evidence: The text explicitly states this assessment of the Keshishian study.

claim: In-depth analysis of clinically-relevant-sized plasma cohorts remains a challenge despite advances in the field.
source: However, despite these advances in the field, in-depth analysis of clinically-relevant-sized plasma cohorts remains a challenge.
evidence: The text states this as a current limitation in the field.

claim: HiRIEF LC-MS/MS has demonstrated capability of in-depth proteome analysis of cell and tissue samples.
source: High-resolution isoelectric focusing based pre-fractionation prior MS analysis (HiRIEF LC-MS/MS) has demonstrated capability of in-depth proteome analysis of cell and tissue samples (Branca et al., 2014).
evidence: The text cites previous work demonstrating HiRIEF capabilities in cell and tissue analysis.

claim: Only a limited number of studies have applied proteogenomics to plasma.
source: Presently, only a limited number of studies have applied proteogenomics to plasma (Liu et al., 2015; Johansson et al., 2013; Chen et al., 2012) and as of yet, no global studies have been performed to integrate genomic sequence information to the protein sequence variants in plasma to detect SAAV or other protein sequence alterations, as here presented as proof-of-principle.
evidence: The text states this as the current state of the field with citations.

claim: No global studies have been performed to integrate genomic sequence information to the protein sequence variants in plasma to detect SAAV prior to this study.
source: Presently, only a limited number of studies have applied proteogenomics to plasma (Liu et al., 2015; Johansson et al., 2013; Chen et al., 2012) and as of yet, no global studies have been performed to integrate genomic sequence information to the protein sequence variants in plasma to detect SAAV or other protein sequence alterations, as here presented as proof-of-principle.
evidence: The text explicitly states this is the first such study.

claim: An average of 1,505 proteins per condition were identified in the optimization experiments with strict 1% FDR cut-off at PSM, peptide and protein level.
source: When optimizing the HiRIEF methodology we identified on average 1505 proteins per condition (min 904, max 1888), with strict 1% FDR cut-off at PSM, peptide and protein level (Table 1, Supplementary file 1)
evidence: The text reports this as a result from the optimization experiments, with data shown in Table 1.

claim: The MS runtime control identified as few as 241 proteins.
source: In comparison, the MS runtime control identified as few as 241 proteins.
evidence: The text reports this as a comparison to the HiRIEF results, shown in Table 1.

claim: In the runtime control, less than 10 proteins composed 50% of the total protein intensity.
source: In the runtime control, less than 10 proteins composed 50% of the total protein intensity (Figure 1—figure supplement 1a), hence indicating repetitive detection of high-abundance proteins in absence of further fractionation despite having depleted the 14 most abundant proteins.
evidence: The text states this finding with reference to Figure 1—figure supplement 1a.

claim: The pH range did not impact largely on protein identification numbers in the HiRIEF evaluation.
source: From the HiRIEF pH range evaluation of broad (pH 3–10), narrow (pH 3.7–4.9) and ultra-narrow ranges (pH 3.7–4.05, 4.0–4.25, 4.2–4.45), we concluded that the pH range did not impact largely on protein identification numbers, which is in line with previously reported studies using HiRIEF on cells and tissue (Table 1) (Zhu et al., 2018).
evidence: The text states this conclusion from the optimization experiments, with data in Table 1.

claim: Almost twice as many peptides were identified in the broad range compared to the ultra-narrow ranges.
source: However, almost twice as many peptides were identified in the broad range compared to the ultra-narrow ranges, implying its usefulness for peptide-based quantitative analyses.
evidence: The text states this finding from the optimization experiments.

claim: The identification overlap across different pH intervals was larger on protein level than on peptide sequence level.
source: As expected, the identification overlap across the different pH intervals was larger on protein level than on peptide sequence level (Figure 1—figure supplement 1b).
evidence: The text states this finding with reference to Figure 1—figure supplement 1b.

claim: The overlapping proteins between different pH intervals were predominantly annotated as high-abundance plasma proteins.
source: The overlapping proteins between different pH intervals were predominantly annotated as high-abundance plasma proteins (Figure 1—figure supplement 1c–f).
evidence: The text states this finding with reference to Figure 1—figure supplement 1c-f.

claim: There is a correlation between peptide load on the strip and analytical depth.
source: In the second step of the optimization, sample loads on the HiRIEF strip were evaluated in terms of analytical depth (Figure 1b) and protein identification numbers. This analysis clearly shows a correlation between peptide load on the strip and analytical depth, as well as total numbers of identified proteins when comparing 0.2 mg load to 1 mg, but reaching saturation at 4 mg (Figure 1c), a feature which has previously not been shown in cellular/tissue analysis.
evidence: The text states this finding with reference to Figure 1b and 1c.

claim: The correlation between peptide load and analytical depth reaches saturation at 4 mg.
source: This analysis clearly shows a correlation between peptide load on the strip and analytical depth, as well as total numbers of identified proteins when comparing 0.2 mg load to 1 mg, but reaching saturation at 4 mg (Figure 1c), a feature which has previously not been shown in cellular/tissue analysis.
evidence: The text states this finding with reference to Figure 1c.

claim: On average 3.3% of proteins contain phosphorylated peptides across all strips.
source: To explore the potential of plasma phosphoprotein identification in the acidic HiRIEF range (Panizza et al., 2017), we re-searched the data for phosphorylation modifications and found that on average 3.3% of proteins to contain phosphorylated peptides across all strips, including the clinically relevant EGFR.
evidence: The text reports this finding from re-searching the data for phosphorylation modifications.

claim: The highest number of phosphopeptides was found in strips covering the most acidic pI range.
source: The highest number of phosphopeptides was found in strips covering the most acidic pI range (Supplementary file 2).
evidence: The text states this finding from the phosphorylation analysis.

claim: The distribution of protein phosphorylation sites in plasma differs from data from previous intracellular studies, showing a relatively high proportion of phospho-tyrosine and phospho-threonine modifications.
source: Somewhat surprisingly, the distribution of protein phosphorylation sites differed from data from previous intracellular studies, showing a relatively high proportion of phospho-tyrosine and phospho-threonine modifications (Lundby et al., 2012; Olsen et al., 2006; Sharma et al., 2014) (Supplementary file 3).
evidence: The text states this finding comparing plasma phosphorylation patterns to intracellular studies.

claim: In total 3,053 proteins were identified in the optimization experiments.
source: When summarizing the protein identifications from the different loads and pI intervals in total 3053 proteins were identified in the optimization experiments (Supplementary file 4).
evidence: The text reports this total from the optimization experiments.

claim: Plasma HiRIEF has the ability to cover at least 2,236 of the 3,509 proteins reported in the PeptideAtlas using gene centric comparison.
source: A comparison of our data to the 3509 proteins from the most recent version of the human plasma PeptideAtlas data set (Schwenk et al., 2017) shows that by using different pH intervals, plasma HiRIEF has the ability to cover at least 2236 of the 3509 proteins reported in the PeptideAtlas using gene centric comparison (Figure 1—figure supplement 2).
evidence: The text states this comparison with the PeptideAtlas database.

claim: Among the 611 plasma proteins detected exclusively by the HiRIEF approach, Golgi membrane proteins and MHC molecules were enriched.
source: Among the 611 plasma proteins detected exclusively by the HiRIEF approach, Golgi membrane proteins and MHC molecules were enriched (Supplementary file 4).
evidence: The text states this finding from GO enrichment analysis of HiRIEF-unique proteins.

claim: PSA was only detected in the 4.0–4.25 strip and not in the broader 3.7–4.9 or 3–10 strips, despite covering the same pI interval.
source: Interestingly, PSA was only detected in the 4.0–4.25 strip and not in the broader 3.7–4.9 or 3–10 strips, despite covering the same pI interval.
evidence: The text reports this finding from the PSA spike-in experiment.

claim: Specific, narrower pH intervals could be used to increase analytical depth for selected proteins.
source: This implies that specific, narrower pH intervals could be used to increase analytical depth for selected proteins.
evidence: The text infers this conclusion from the PSA detection results.

claim: A slightly higher proportion of intracellular proteins were detected in the ultranarrow ranges.
source: In line with this, analyzing the proportion of extracellular, membrane, cytoplasmic and nuclear proteins detected in the different pH intervals, a slightly higher proportion of intracellular proteins were detected in the ultranarrow ranges (Figure 1—figure supplement 3).
evidence: The text states this finding from analysis of protein subcellular localization.

claim: 670 × 10−18 moles of the PSA peptide were detected in the MRM analysis.
source: In the experiment, we detected 670 × 10−18 moles of the PSA peptide, demonstrating that findings from the global analysis can be validated using targeted MS-methods by rational selection of HiRIEF fractions based on theoretical peptide pI (Figure 1—figure supplement 4a–b).
evidence: The text reports this quantification from the MRM validation experiment.

claim: In total 2,587 unique proteins were identified across the TMT-sets in the first cohort.
source: We identified in total 2587 unique proteins across the TMT-sets, of which 1313 (51%) were detected in all four sets (Figure 1—figure supplement 6b).
evidence: The text reports this result from the first TMT cohort analysis.

claim: 1,313 proteins (51%) were detected in all four TMT sets in the first cohort.
source: We identified in total 2587 unique proteins across the TMT-sets, of which 1313 (51%) were detected in all four sets (Figure 1—figure supplement 6b).
evidence: The text reports this result showing reproducibility across TMT sets.

claim: The average peptide level technical CV within one TMT set was 4.7%.
source: The average peptide level technical CV (coefficient of variation) within one TMT set was 4.7% and the average CV between sets was of 7.3% (Figure 1—figure supplement 6c,d).
evidence: The text reports this reproducibility metric from the TMT analysis.

claim: The average CV between TMT sets was 7.3%.
source: The average peptide level technical CV (coefficient of variation) within one TMT set was 4.7% and the average CV between sets was of 7.3% (Figure 1—figure supplement 6c,d).
evidence: The text reports this reproducibility metric from the TMT analysis.

claim: In the second cohort, 2,123 proteins were identified in total.
source: To test this condensed approach, we analyzed a second longitudinal cohort with plasma samples from 12 women making a total of five TMT-sets. In this analysis, we identified in total 2123 proteins, with 1135 being detected in in all five sets, showing that the reduced analysis time only had a minor impact on the number of identified proteins (Figure 1—figure supplement 7a,b,c,d).
evidence: The text reports this result from the second cohort analysis.

claim: 1,135 proteins were detected in all five TMT sets in the second cohort.
source: In this analysis, we identified in total 2123 proteins, with 1135 being detected in in all five sets, showing that the reduced analysis time only had a minor impact on the number of identified proteins (Figure 1—figure supplement 7a,b,c,d).
evidence: The text reports this result showing reproducibility in the condensed approach.

claim: The reduced analysis time only had a minor impact on the number of identified proteins.
source: In this analysis, we identified in total 2123 proteins, with 1135 being detected in in all five sets, showing that the reduced analysis time only had a minor impact on the number of identified proteins (Figure 1—figure supplement 7a,b,c,d).
evidence: The text states this conclusion comparing the condensed approach to the full analysis.

claim: 828 genes were identified in all nine TMT sets containing samples from 42 individuals.
source: Using this approach, we identified in total 828 genes in all nine TMT sets containing samples from 42 individuals (both men and women) (Figure 1—figure supplement 7e).
evidence: The text reports this core set of robustly detected proteins across all cohorts.

claim: Keshishian et al. report between 2,066 and 4,836 proteins identified per set, depending on the labelling approach and experiment.
source: Starting from 400 μl of plasma per sample and performing extensive IgY-based depletion in combination with high-pH reversed phase prefractionation into 30 fractions, Keshishian et al. report between 2066 and 4836 proteins identified per set, depending on the labelling approach and experiment, using approximately 90 hr of MS-time per set.
evidence: The text cites these results from the Keshishian study for benchmarking.

claim: Keshishian et al. present median peptide level CVs between 16–24% across different abundance ranges based on spiked-in peptides.
source: Based on spiked-in peptides they present median peptide level CVs between 16–24% across different abundance ranges.
evidence: The text cites these reproducibility metrics from the Keshishian study for comparison.

claim: 1,394 genes were robustly identified in all seven sets from the Keshishian data.
source: Performing the same gene-centric core-set analysis, as described above for the HiRIEF data, on the re-searched data from the four iTRAQ 4-plex sets (four patients) and the iTRAQ 4-plex, TMT-6 plex, TMT-10 plex analysis (one pooled plasma sample), a set of 1394 genes was robustly identified in all seven sets.
evidence: The text reports this result from re-analysis of the Keshishian data.

claim: 1,043 genes were identified in seven out of the nine HiRIEF sets.
source: In comparison to our data, we identified 1043 genes in seven out of the nine sets, with 42 individuals, starting with 40 μl plasma and 14-protein MARS depletion (Figure 1—figure supplement 7e).
evidence: The text reports this result for comparison with the Keshishian data.

claim: Coagulation- and complement cascade proteins such as complement factor I (CF1) and complement component C6 were tightly regulated.
source: When examining the classes of proteins associated with low or high variability by comparative GO enrichment analyses, we found that coagulation- and complement cascade proteins such as complement factor I (CF1) and complement component C6 were tightly regulated, which was in line with previous findings (Cominetti et al., 2016).
evidence: The text states this finding from the inter-individual variability analysis.

claim: Transmembrane proteins and proteins coupled to receptor activity, such as EGFR and TGFBR3, were tightly regulated.
source: Interestingly, transmembrane proteins and proteins coupled to receptor activity, such as the cancer-related EGFR and TGFBR3, were also tightly regulated (Supplementary file 5).
evidence: The text states this finding from the inter-individual variability analysis.

claim: Large inter-individual variation was observed for lipoproteins and keratins.
source: Large inter-individual variation was observed for lipoproteins and keratins (the latter classified as probable contamination) (Supplementary file 6).
evidence: The text states this finding from the inter-individual variability analysis.

claim: Lipoprotein A (LPA) showed large variability between individuals.
source: One example of proteins with large variability between individuals was lipoprotein A (LPA), for which a genetic variation affecting its secretion into plasma is known (Boerwinkle et al., 1989; Utermann, 1989) (Figure 2a).
evidence: The text states this finding with reference to known genetic variation.

claim: A genetic variation affecting lipoprotein A secretion into plasma is known.
source: One example of proteins with large variability between individuals was lipoprotein A (LPA), for which a genetic variation affecting its secretion into plasma is known (Boerwinkle et al., 1989; Utermann, 1989) (Figure 2a).
evidence: The text cites this as known information about LPA.

claim: HLA genes are highly polymorphic and showed very high level of variability.
source: The HLA genes are similarly known to be highly polymorphic and showed very high level of variability, which could be due to the fact that the peptides were not properly assigned to the reference sequences in the database search.
evidence: The text states this finding with a possible explanation for the high variability.

claim: APOC2 and CETP showed strong gender correlation, with lower concentrations in women.
source: Two other highly variable proteins (APOC2 and CETP) showed strong gender correlation, with lower concentrations in women (Figure 2b).
evidence: The text states this finding from the gender comparison analysis.

claim: Increased levels of CETP in women with Type two diabetes, but not in men, has been coupled to cardiovascular disease.
source: Increased levels of CETP in women with Type two diabetes, but not in men, has been coupled to cardiovascular disease (Alssema et al., 2007).
evidence: The text cites this as known information about CETP and cardiovascular disease.

claim: Unsupervised clustering of the data showed distinct gender effects in the plasma proteome.
source: Unsupervised clustering of the data showed distinct gender effects in the plasma proteome (Figure 2c), that are concordant with previous studies (Corzett et al., 2010; Miike et al., 2010).
evidence: The text states this finding from clustering analysis, with citations to previous studies.

claim: The major gender-correlated cluster with relative up-regulation in male subjects contained proteins linked to lipid transport and binding.
source: Interestingly, the major gender-correlated cluster with relative up-regulation in male subjects contained proteins linked to lipid transport and binding.
evidence: The text states this finding from the clustering and GO enrichment analysis.

claim: 15 of the 38 proteins in the gender-correlated cluster with significant differential expression were proteins implicated as candidate cardiovascular disease genes.
source: In fact, 15 of the 38 proteins in the cluster with significant gender-specific differential expression (Student's t-test, p<0.01, FDR corrected) were proteins implicated as candidate cardiovascular disease genes, including seven potential drug targets and two FDA-approved drug targets (classification according to the ProteinAtlas, www.proteinatlas.org) (Figure 2d, Figure 2—figure supplement 2).
evidence: The text states this finding from analysis of the gender-correlated cluster.

claim: Five out of eight proteins from the CancerSEEK test were identified in the optimization experiments.
source: We identified five out of eight proteins in the optimization experiments (covering several pI intervals) and three of eight proteins in the cohort consisting of 30 healthy plasma donors analyzed only on the 3–10 strip (Figure 3a, Supplementary file 7).
evidence: The text reports this result from mining the data for CancerSEEK proteins.

claim: Three of eight proteins from the CancerSEEK test were identified in the cohort of 30 healthy plasma donors.
source: We identified five out of eight proteins in the optimization experiments (covering several pI intervals) and three of eight proteins in the cohort consisting of 30 healthy plasma donors analyzed only on the 3–10 strip (Figure 3a, Supplementary file 7).
evidence: The text reports this result from the 30-donor cohort analysis.

claim: Classical plasma proteins were detected in the high-abundance range.
source: As expected, classical plasma proteins were detected in the high-abundance range and potential biomarker classes (FDA-approved drug targets, cancer-related proteins, the proteins from the CancerSEEK test and the spiked PSA) were detected in the lower abundance ranges (Figure 3b, Figure 3—figure supplement 1, and Supplementary file 8).
evidence: The text states this expected finding from the abundance analysis.

claim: Potential biomarker classes were detected in the lower abundance ranges.
source: As expected, classical plasma proteins were detected in the high-abundance range and potential biomarker classes (FDA-approved drug targets, cancer-related proteins, the proteins from the CancerSEEK test and the spiked PSA) were detected in the lower abundance ranges (Figure 3b, Figure 3—figure supplement 1, and Supplementary file 8).
evidence: The text states this finding from the abundance analysis.

claim: Using plasma HiRIEF, over 500 tissue-enriched proteins were detected spanning over a wide range of concentrations.
source: Notably, using plasma HiRIEF, we could detect over 500 tissue-enriched proteins spanning over a wide range of concentrations, from highly abundant plasma proteins produced in the liver to less abundant proteins produced in the central nervous system or the pancreas (Figure 3c, Figure 3—figure supplement 1, and Supplementary file 8).
evidence: The text reports this finding from the tissue leakage protein analysis.

claim: Eight proteins classified as placental enriched were detected at low levels in the cohort with 30 blood donors (non-pregnant).
source: In this cohort, we detected low levels of eight proteins classified as placental enriched (median #PSMs 2, range 0–21, the outlier protein IGF2; Figure 4a).
evidence: The text reports this finding from the non-pregnant cohort as a negative control.

claim: 30 tissue enriched placental proteins were detected in plasma during pregnancy.
source: During pregnancy, we could detect 30 tissue enriched placental proteins in plasma, with median # of PSM´s 46 (range 1–424), which were not detected, or detected at low levels prior to pregnancy (median #of PSMs 0, range 0–31, again the outlier protein being IGF2) (Figure 4b).
evidence: The text reports this finding from the pregnancy sample analysis.

claim: Over 30 placenta-enriched proteins were found at high levels in maternal plasma in the mother-newborn pairs.
source: In this cohort we found over 30 placenta-enriched proteins at high levels in the maternal plasma (Figure 4c), but only a small increase of placental proteins among the newborns, with a median PSM ratio mother:newborn of 4:1 and 5:1, respectively.
evidence: The text reports this finding from the mother-newborn comparison.

claim: Only a small increase of placental proteins was observed among the newborns, with a median PSM ratio mother:newborn of 4:1 and 5:1.
source: In this cohort we found over 30 placenta-enriched proteins at high levels in the maternal plasma (Figure 4c), but only a small increase of placental proteins among the newborns, with a median PSM ratio mother:newborn of 4:1 and 5:1, respectively.
evidence: The text reports this finding from the mother-newborn comparison.

claim: Anti-Mullerian-Hormone (AMH) was uniquely detected in both babies.
source: Among the proteins uniquely detected in both babies were Anti-Mullerian-Hormone (AMH), which has reported serum level concentrations of 52 ng/mL in newborn boys (Bergadá et al., 2006) (both newborns were boys) compared to approximately 2 ng/mL in females during pregnancy and puerperium (La Marca et al., 2005).
evidence: The text reports this finding with citations to known AMH concentrations.

claim: AMH has reported serum level concentrations of 52 ng/mL in newborn boys.
source: Among the proteins uniquely detected in both babies were Anti-Mullerian-Hormone (AMH), which has reported serum level concentrations of 52 ng/mL in newborn boys (Bergadá et al., 2006) (both newborns were boys) compared to approximately 2 ng/mL in females during pregnancy and puerperium (La Marca et al., 2005).
evidence: The text cites this known concentration of AMH in newborn boys.
